Consequently, the few existing SNN models (Kim, Chough, and Panda ; Zhang, Fan, and Zhang ; Yao et al. 2024a; Su et al. ; Patel et al. ) that tackle image segmentation tasks tend to perform poorly. This work explores the application of SNNs with more complex architectures to image segmentation tasks. Specifically, Mask2Former (Cheng et al. ) is a classic Transformer-based per-mask classification architecture consisting of three parts: a backbone network; a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) pixel decoder with a multi-scale deformable transformer encoder block; and a transformer decoder block. To address this, we investigated which modules in the spiking Mask2Former contribute to the significant loss of information, where the spiking neurons in these modules nearly cease to fire. The first module with severe spike degradation is the deformable attention transformer encoder block in the FPN decoder. To address this, we incorporate convolution blocks in encoder blocks and redesign the deformable attention blocks to preserve more effective information and energy efficiency. The second key module that leads to information loss is the final mask embedding layer. To end this, we build an auxiliary information branch to enhance the representation of mask embedding.
